mainTopic: Which wine רב's rule excludes from קידוש, the preference for red wine, and a new משנה on selling wine that sours
overview: The גמרא continues working on רב's rule that wine פסול for the מזבח is also פסול for קידוש היום. It asks what kind of wine this rule is meant to exclude. Fresh juice, wine from the top or bottom of the barrel, and lower-quality wines are all rejected, because they are fine for קידוש or valid בדיעבד on the מזבח. The גמרא then points to wines that are פסול even בדיעבד: souring, diluted, uncovered, dregs, and bad-smelling wine. It asks which of these רב really needed to teach, and knocks out four of them one by one. It ends with bad-smelling wine, or, in a second answer, uncovered wine that was strained, which is safe but still disrespectful for a מצוה. רבא then uses a פסוק to show that red wine is preferred over white. The גמרא adds a ברייתא about the inferior jugs from the שרון. Finally, a new משנה begins about a seller whose wine turns sour after the sale, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Freshly squeezed grape juice is fine for kiddush
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the earlier suggestion that רב's rule excludes fresh wine straight from the press. רבא says one may squeeze grapes and make קידוש on the juice right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא says: A person may squeeze a cluster of grapes and recite קידוש היום over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא to show that brand-new, freshly squeezed juice is good for קידוש. So רב's rule cannot be coming to exclude it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier suggestion was that רב's rule excludes fresh wine from the press. רבא says this kind of wine works for קידוש, so that suggestion fails and the גמרא needs a new answer.

keyTerms.meaning: the קידוש said over wine on שבת or יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of an argument from the previous page. The word דְּאָמַר ("as he says") tells you it is the proof for a rejection that already began there.
steps.whyThisMatters: In הלכה, fresh grape juice can be used for קידוש.

phrases.english: As Rava says:
A person may squeeze a cluster of grapes,
and recite the sanctification of the day over it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous page's suggestion that רב excludes fresh wine from the press.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רב's rule excludes freshly pressed wine.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא rules that freshly squeezed juice is valid for קידוש.

steps.title: New suggestion: wine from the top or bottom of the barrel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב's rule excludes wine taken from the top of the barrel or from the bottom of the barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, maybe רב's rule comes to exclude wine from the barrel's mouth and from its bottom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new answer to "what does רב's rule exclude?" This sets up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine at the top of a barrel has scum floating in it. Wine at the bottom has the leftover grape mush. Maybe these are what רב meant as unfit for the מזבח and so also unfit for קידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (introduces a new suggestion after one failed)
from its mouth, the top of the barrel
from its bottom, the lowest part of the barrel

phrases.english: Rather, to exclude wine from its mouth and from its bottom?
phrases.notes: "Its" means the wine barrel. The top has scum and the bottom has sediment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first suggestion was rejected, a new one is offered.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב's rule excludes wine from the top or bottom of the barrel.

steps.title: Rabbi Chiya: top and bottom wine is valid after the fact
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא taught that wine from the top or bottom of the barrel is כשר בדיעבד on the מזבח. So it is not truly פסול for the מזבח, and רב's rule would not exclude it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי חייא taught: One should not bring wine from the barrel's mouth or bottom, but if he did bring it, it is כשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new suggestion with a teaching of רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule only excludes wine that is truly פסול for the מזבח. Top and bottom wine is valid if it was already brought, so it counts as כשר and should also be fine for קידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't he teach (opens a challenge from a teaching)
he should not bring (it is not ideal to begin with, לכתחילה)
but if he brought it, it is valid (בדיעבד)

steps.confusionAlert: "Don't bring it" does not mean פסול. Here the wine is only discouraged at the start. Once it was brought it counts, and that is why it is not excluded.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Chiya teach:
From its mouth and from its bottom one should not bring,
phrases.notes: "Bring" means bring as a wine offering on the מזבח.

phrases.english: but if he brought it, it is valid!

steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רב's rule excludes top and bottom wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That wine is כשר בדיעבד for the מזבח, so it is not פסול there and רב's rule cannot be excluding it.

steps.title: New suggestion: black, pale, sweet, cellar, or raisin wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now suggests that רב's rule excludes certain lower-quality kinds of wine: black wine, borek wine, sweet wine, cellar wine, and raisin wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, maybe רב's rule excludes black wine, borek wine, heiliston (sweet) wine, cellar wine, and raisin wine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third answer for what רב's rule excludes. This sets up another challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These wines are not standard, top-quality wine. Maybe they are what רב meant as unfit for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: borek, a white wine of poor quality, as Rashbam explains

phrases.english: Rather, to exclude black wine;
borek wine; sweet wine;
wine of the cellar; wine of raisins?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 3 rejected the previous suggestion, a new list is proposed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב's rule excludes black, borek, sweet, cellar, and raisin wine.

steps.title: A ברייתא says these wines are also valid after the fact
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that all these wines are כשר בדיעבד on the מזבח. So רב's rule cannot be excluding them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: With all of these, one should not bring them, but if he did bring them, they are כשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the third suggestion the same way it knocked down the second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge follows the same pattern as step 3. Because these wines work בדיעבד on the מזבח, they are not truly פסול there, so they should be fine for קידוש too.

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
With all of them, one should not bring,
but if he brought it, it is valid!

steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רב's rule excludes black, borek, sweet, cellar, and raisin wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These wines are כשר בדיעבד for the מזבח, so they fall outside a rule about wine that is פסול for the מזבח.

steps.title: Fourth suggestion: wines that are disqualified even after the fact
steps.stepSummary: רב's rule excludes souring, diluted, uncovered, dregs, and bad-smelling wine. A ברייתא says these are פסול on the מזבח even בדיעבד, so they are also unfit for קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב's rule excludes souring wine, diluted wine, uncovered wine, wine made from the dregs, and bad-smelling wine. As a ברייתא teaches: With all of these, one should not bring them, and if he did bring them, they are פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a fourth suggestion and backs it up with a ברייתא. This time the wines are disqualified even after the fact. The next step will ask which of these wines רב's rule is really needed for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now every suggestion failed because the wine was valid בדיעבד. These wines are פסול even בדיעבד, so they are truly unfit for the מזבח, and רב's rule makes them unfit for קידוש as well.

keyTerms.meaning: souring, starting to turn to vinegar
dregs, grape leftovers at the bottom

steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule only covers wine that is פסול on the מזבח even בדיעבד. Wine that is merely not ideal (לכתחילה) is still fine for קידוש. Steps 7-13 then narrow down which wine on this list רב's rule actually excludes.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the test for רב's rule: only wine that is פסול on the מזבח even after the fact. The following steps check each item on this list against that test.

phrases.english: Rather, to exclude souring wine;
diluted wine; uncovered wine;
phrases.notes: Uncovered wine is a worry because a snake may have put venom in it.

phrases.english: and wine of the dregs; and wine whose smell is bad –
as it is taught:
With all of them, one should not bring,
and if he brought it, it is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two failed suggestions, offers a third list, with support from a ברייתא. Step 7 then asks which item on it רב's rule really targets.
steps.raayaObject: That these wines are truly פסול for the מזבח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא ruling them פסול even בדיעבד.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב's rule refers to wines that are פסול for the מזבח even בדיעבד; steps 7–13 narrow down which one.

steps.title: Which of these wines did רב really mean to exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the five unfit wines רב's rule is actually meant to exclude.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב's rule comes to exclude which wine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about the list from step 6. This is a setup line: next it will test each kind of wine one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 gave a list of wines that are פסול on the מזבח even בדיעבד. Now the גמרא wants to know which one רב actually needed to teach us. It wants a case where his rule adds something new.

keyTerms.meaning: to exclude; what a rule comes to leave out

phrases.english: To exclude what?
phrases.notes: He means: which of the five wines from the list does רב's rule come to rule out for קידוש?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the conclusion of step 6 by asking which item on its list רב's rule really needed to teach.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific wine רב's rule comes to exclude from קידוש.

steps.title: Souring wine is already a known dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב's rule cannot be meant for souring wine, because that wine is already the subject of a dispute between רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say רב's rule excludes souring wine, that is a dispute between רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, souring wine (קוסס). It rejects it because the status of this wine is already argued about by two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether souring wine counts as wine is a known מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי. So it is not a simple, clear case that רב's rule could be pointing to.

keyTerms.meaning: wine that is starting to sour

phrases.english: If it is to exclude souring wine,
it is a dispute of רבי יוחנן
phrases.notes: This dispute came up earlier in the סוגיא, about wine that tastes like wine but smells like vinegar.

phrases.english: and רבי יהושע בן לוי!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first candidate answer to the question of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רב's rule excludes souring wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Souring wine's status is already a disputed matter, so it cannot be the clear case רב's rule is pointing to.

steps.title: Diluted wine is actually better for a blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב's rule cannot be meant for diluted wine, because adding water improves wine. Even the חכמים agree that a כוס של ברכה needs water added.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say רב's rule excludes diluted wine, that is an improvement for it! As רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא said: the חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר about a cup of blessing, that one does not bless on it until he puts water into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second option, diluted wine (מזוג). It rejects it because water makes wine better for a ברכה, not worse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא brings proof from רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא. Even the חכמים, who disagree with רבי אליעזר elsewhere, agree that a כוס של ברכה should have water added before the ברכה. So diluted wine is the preferred way to make קידוש, and רב could not be excluding it.

keyTerms.meaning: a cup of wine used for a ברכה, like ברכת המזון

steps.confusionAlert: On the מזבח, diluted wine is פסול. But for drinking and for a ברכה, water is what makes the wine good. Do not mix up the two settings.

phrases.english: If it is to exclude diluted wine,
that is an improvement for it,
as רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא said:
The חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר
about a cup of blessing,
that one does not make the blessing over it
until he puts water into it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the second candidate from the list of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רב's rule excludes diluted wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Water improves wine for a ברכה, as רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא proves. So diluted wine cannot be unfit for קידוש.

steps.title: Uncovered wine is already forbidden as dangerous
steps.stepSummary: רב's rule is not needed for uncovered wine, because that wine is already forbidden as a danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say רב's rule excludes uncovered wine, it is a danger!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the third option, uncovered wine (מגולה). It rejects it because such wine is already off-limits, since drinking it is dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine left uncovered may not be drunk at all because of סכנה. Nobody would use it for קידוש anyway, so רב did not need a special rule to exclude it.

phrases.english: If it is to exclude uncovered wine,
it is a danger!
phrases.notes: The worry is that a snake drank from it and left venom inside, so it is forbidden to drink anyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the third candidate from the list of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רב's rule excludes uncovered wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Uncovered wine is already forbidden because of danger, so רב's rule would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: Dregs wine is either real wine or already disputed
steps.stepSummary: רב's rule cannot be meant for wine made from dregs. If more liquid came out than the water put in, it is real wine. If only a little more came out, it is a known dispute between the רבנן and אחרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say רב's rule excludes wine from dregs, what is the case? If he poured three and four came out, it is real wine! If he poured three and three and a half came out, it is a dispute of the רבנן and אחרים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the fourth option, wine made by pouring water over dregs (שמרים). It asks what the case is and shows that both ways of reading it fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If three measures of water produced four, the extra measure is real wine taken from the dregs. Such a drink counts as good wine and is fine for קידוש. If three produced only three and a half, whether it counts as wine is already a מחלוקת between the רבנן and אחרים, so רב's rule cannot simply be pointing to it.

keyTerms.meaning: dregs; the leftover grape matter at the bottom of the wine
what is the case? how exactly does it look?
a תנא quoted by this name, disputing the רבנן

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא went through the step 6 list one at a time: souring (already disputed), diluted (actually better), uncovered (already forbidden), dregs (real wine or already disputed). None of these four works, and the next step gives the answer.

phrases.english: If it is to exclude wine of dregs,
what is the case?
If he poured three and four came out,
phrases.notes: He poured three jugs of water onto the dregs. Four came out, so a whole extra jug of wine came from the dregs.

phrases.english: it is good wine!
If he poured three
and three and a half came out,
it is a dispute of the Rabbis and אחרים!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לְמַעוֹטֵי שֶׁל שְׁמָרִים, הֵיכִי דָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the fourth candidate from the list of step 6, using a two-sided question about the case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רב's rule excludes wine made from dregs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both ways of reading the case fail. In the four-from-three case it is good wine, fit for קידוש. In the three-and-a-half case its status is already disputed, so רב's rule cannot be pointing to it.

steps.title: רב's rule excludes wine with a bad smell
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting the other options, the גמרא concludes that רב's rule is meant to exclude wine that smells bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב's rule comes to exclude wine that has a bad smell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally answers the question from step 7. רב's rule is meant to exclude wine with a bad smell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 8 to 11 knocked out souring, diluted, uncovered and dregs wine. The only remaining case is wine that smells bad. The גמרא raises no objection to this case: it is not already disputed, not an improvement, and not already forbidden for another reason. So this is what רב's rule teaches.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to exclude
wine that has a bad smell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 after the rejections in steps 8 to 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב's rule excludes wine with a bad smell.

steps.title: Or רב's rule excludes uncovered wine even after it was strained
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: רב's rule really excludes uncovered wine. It teaches that even if the wine was strained through a sieve, so it is no longer dangerous according to רבי נחמיה, it is still too disrespectful to use for a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer: the rule really excludes uncovered wine. Even though someone passed it through a strainer, as רבי נחמיה allows, it is still unfit. As the פסוק says: 'Offer it to your governor; will he be pleased with you or show you favor?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer. It goes back to uncovered wine, which step 10 had rejected, and shows that רב's rule still teaches something new about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said uncovered wine is already forbidden because it is dangerous. Here the גמרא answers that if the wine was strained, then according to רבי נחמיה the danger is gone. Even so, רב's rule teaches that it is still unfit for קידוש, because it is disrespectful to bring something you would not give to a human ruler.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you prefer, say (an alternative answer)

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers: רב excludes wine that smells bad, or uncovered wine even after straining. Wine that is safe can still be too lowly to use for a מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up a principle: a מצוה needs wine that is respectable, not just wine that is safe to drink.

phrases.english: And if you prefer, say:
really, it comes to exclude uncovered wine,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the option that step 10 had rejected.

phrases.english: and even though he passed it
through a strainer, as רבי נחמיה holds,
even so, it is unfit, because:
'Offer it now to your governor;
will he be pleased with you or show you favor?'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 7 by undoing the rejection in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: strained uncovered wine, which is safe but still disrespectful.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Uncovered wine is already forbidden as dangerous, so רב would not need to mention it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once strained, it is not dangerous, yet it is still unfit for a מצוה because of disrespect.

steps.title: Is white wine acceptable?
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא asks רבא what the law is for white wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא, the father-in-law of רב משרשיא, asked רבא: What is the law about white wine?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רב כהנא asks רבא whether white wine may be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the discussion was about wine that is damaged or spoiled. White wine is not damaged; it is just a different kind. So the question is whether color alone affects its quality for a מצוה.

phrases.english: רב כהנא asked
the father-in-law of Rav Mesharshiyya, of Rava:
White wine, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא חֲמוּהּ דְּרַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא מֵרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related question about which wines are fit.

steps.title: רבא answers: red wine is the preferred wine
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a פסוק showing that red wine is the most desirable wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Do not look at wine when it is red.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers with a פסוק from משלי that describes red wine as the tempting, attractive kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק warns against staring at red wine, so red must be the most appealing wine. This suggests red wine is the higher quality and the preferred choice.

phrases.english: He said to him:
'Do not look at wine when it is red.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַל תֵּרֶא יַיִן כִּי יִתְאַדָּם
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Red wine is the preferred kind, as shown by the פסוק.

steps.title: Even the inferior jugs from the Sharon must be decent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about jugs from the שרון and adds a ברייתא: the inferior jugs the buyer must accept must still be nice-looking and sealed with pitch.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Jugs in the שרון, etc.' A ברייתא taught: these are inferior jugs that are still nice and sealed with pitch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's rule that a buyer of jugs in the שרון must accept up to ten bad jugs per hundred. A ברייתא limits this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה made the buyer accept some inferior jugs. The ברייתא adds that this applies only if those jugs still look good and are sealed with pitch. Jugs that are truly poor are not included in the allowance.

phrases.english: The משנה said: 'Jugs in the שרון, etc.'
phrases.notes: The משנה says a buyer there must accept ten inferior jugs in a hundred.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא:
inferior jugs that are nice-looking and sealed with pitch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The inferior jugs the buyer must accept must still be nice-looking and sealed with pitch.

steps.title: New משנה: selling wine that later turns sour
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if wine sours after the sale, the seller is not responsible. But if his wine is known to sour, the sale is a mistaken sale. The משנה then begins a new case about a seller who says 'wine...'.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone sells wine to another and it turns sour, the seller is not responsible for it. But if it is known that his wine turns sour, it is a mistaken sale. And if he said to him: 'Wine...'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about whether a seller is responsible when wine sours after it was sold. The last line is cut off, and the משנה continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, souring after the sale is the buyer's bad luck. If this seller's wine is known to sour, the buyer was misled from the start, so the sale can be cancelled. The words 'and if he said to him: wine' open a third case that continues next time.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. Ordinary souring after the sale is the buyer's loss. Only a seller whose wine is known to sour makes it a mistaken sale.

phrases.english: משנה:
One who sells wine to another, and it turned sour,
the seller is not responsible for it.
But if it is known that his wine turns sour,
this is a mistaken sale.
And if he said to him: 'Wine...'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seller is not responsible if wine sours after the sale, unless his wine is known to sour, in which case it is a mistaken sale.
